en: Dhātukathā 2 Niddesa 2.3.
The Third Method: Exposition of Terms Concerning What is Not Included and What is Included.

Those phenomena that are associated with the aggregate of feeling … those phenomena that are associated with the aggregate of perception … those phenomena that are associated with the aggregate of mental formations …

Those phenomena which, by way of the truth of the origin and the truth of the path, are not included in the aggregate-grouping but are included in the base-grouping and the element-grouping: by how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are those phenomena included?
Excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates, those phenomena are included by three aggregates, by one base, and by one element.

Those phenomena that, by way of the truth of cessation (*nirodhasacca*), are not included in the aggregate-grouping (*khandha-saṅgaha*) but are included in the base-grouping (*āyatana-saṅgaha*) and included in the element-grouping (*dhātu-saṅgaha*) … [and so on] … those phenomena are included in four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena that,
by way of the life-faculty (*jīvitindriya*), are not included in the aggregate-grouping but are included in the base-grouping and included in the element-grouping … [and so on] …
Those states, excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates, are comprised within two aggregates, one base, and one element.
Those states [associated] with the female faculty...
those states [associated] with the male faculty...
Those phenomena associated with the faculty of pleasure … those phenomena associated with the faculty of pain … those phenomena associated with the faculty of mental joy …
Those phenomena associated with the faculty of mental distress … those phenomena associated with the faculty of equanimity … those phenomena associated with the faculty of faith …
Those phenomena [arisen] through the faculty of energy … those phenomena [arisen] through the faculty of mindfulness … those phenomena [arisen] through the faculty of concentration …

Those phenomena associated with the faculty of wisdom (paññindriya) … those phenomena associated with the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya) … those phenomena associated with the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya) …
Those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of one who has final knowledge;
those phenomena [associated] with ignorance;
those phenomena [associated] with volitional formations conditioned by ignorance.
Those phenomena that [arise] through contact conditioned by the six sense bases;
those phenomena that [arise] through feeling conditioned by contact;
those phenomena that [arise] through craving conditioned by feeling.
Those phenomena which, conditioned by craving and through clinging,
are not included in the aggregate of kamma-existence (kammabhava), but are included in the inclusion of bases (āyatana) and included in the inclusion of elements (dhātu)—
setting aside the unconditioned as an aggregate— these phenomena are included by three aggregates, one base, and one element.
Those phenomena that [arise] through birth...
those phenomena that [arise] through aging...
those phenomena that [arise] through death...
Those phenomena which, by way of jhāna, are not included in the aggregate-grouping but are included in the base-grouping and included in the element-grouping … [as before] … those phenomena,

setting aside the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates, are included in two aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, by way of sorrow … [as before] … are included in two aggregates, one base, and one element.
Those phenomena that [arise] through suffering … those phenomena that [arise] through mental grief … those phenomena that [arise] through despair …
The states that [are developed] by means of the foundations of mindfulness...
the states that [are developed] by means of the right efforts...
the states that [are developed] by means of the immeasurables...
Those phenomena [associated] with the five faculties...
those phenomena [associated] with the five powers...
those phenomena [associated] with the seven factors of enlightenment...
Those phenomena that [arise] through the noble eightfold path;
those phenomena that [arise] through contact;
those phenomena that [arise] through feeling.
Those phenomena that are associated with perception … those phenomena that are associated with volition … those phenomena that are associated with resolve …
Those phenomena by way of attention;
those phenomena by way of causal factors;
those phenomena by way of both causal factors and factors accompanied by causes.

Those phenomena which, by way of cause and by way of phenomena associated with causes, are not included in the aggregate-inclusion but are included in the base-inclusion and included in the element-inclusion … [as before] … those phenomena,
setting aside the unconditioned from the perspective of aggregates, are included in three aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which,
by way of non-conditions … [as before] … are included in three aggregates, one base, and one element.

Those phenomena which, among the unconditioned phenomena, are not included by the inclusion of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*), but are included by the inclusion of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*) and included by the inclusion of elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*) … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the taints (*āsava*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the outflows (*āsava*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the bonds (*gantha*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the ties (*ogaḷha*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the hindrances (*nīvaraṇa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the latent tendencies (*anusaya*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the perversions (*parāmāsa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the floods (*ogha*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the bonds (*yoga*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the clingings (*kleśa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the corruptions (*kilesa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states conducive to the unwholesome (*akusalapakkhika*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states conducive to the indeterminate (*abyākata*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states conducive to the lower realm (*pariyāpanna*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states not conducive to the lower realm (*apariyāpanna*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states without applied thought and without sustained thought (*avitakkāvicāra*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states with rapture (*pītisahagata*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states accompanied by pleasure (*sukhasahagata*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states accompanied by equanimity (*upekkhāsahagata*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states with limited objects (*parittārammaṇa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states with lofty objects (*mahaggatārammaṇa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states with infinite objects (*appamāṇārammaṇa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states with internal objects (*ajjhattārammaṇa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states with external objects (*bahiddhārammaṇa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are both internal and external objects (*ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are neither internal nor external objects (*na-ajjhatta-na-bahiddhārammaṇa*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are past (*atīta*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are future (*anāgata*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are present (*paccuppanna*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are internal (*ajjhatta*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are external (*bahiddhā*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are both internal and external (*ajjhattabahiddhā*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are neither internal nor external (*na-ajjhatta-na-bahiddhā*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are supramundane (*lokuttara*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are with taints (*sāsava*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are without taints (*anāsava*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are conditioned (*saṅkhata*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are mundane (*lokiya*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are supramundane (*lokuttara*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are with taints (*sāsava*), are … [as before] … those phenomena are included by four aggregates, one base, and one element. Those phenomena which, among the states that are without taints (*anāsava*), are … [as before] … those phenomena
Those phenomena which, by way of the aggregates, are not included among those phenomena that are both taints and subject to taints;

and those phenomena which, by way of the aggregates, are not included among those phenomena that are both taints and associated with taints, yet are included by way of the bases and included by way of the elements—
those phenomena, setting aside the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates, are included by three aggregates, one base, and one element.
By means of the fetters … the ties … the floods …
Those phenomena which, through the applications of mindfulness, the hindrances, or the perversions...

Those phenomena which, by way of the aggregates, are not included among the states associated with the perversions (*parāmāsa*) and those states affected by the perversions, but are included by way of the bases (*āyatana*) and included by way of the elements (*dhātu*)—
setting aside the unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) from the perspective of the aggregates— those phenomena are included by three aggregates, one base, and one element.
Those phenomena which [are not included] among the mental factors (*cetasika*)…
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena associated with consciousness;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena conjoined with consciousness;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena conjoined with and originated by consciousness.
Those phenomena which, by way of the aggregates, are not included among those phenomena that are conjoined with, originated by, and co-existent with the mind;
nor are they included among those phenomena that follow after what is conjoined with and originated by the mind—but which are included by way of the bases and included by way of the elements:
setting aside the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates, those phenomena are included by one aggregate, one base, and one element.
Those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*),

are not included among the phenomena coexistent with consciousness (*cittasahabhū*) or among the phenomena that follow after consciousness (*cittānuparivatti*), but are included by the inclusion of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*) and included by the inclusion of elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*)—
those phenomena are not included by any aggregates, but are included by one base and one element.
Those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena that are objects of clinging;
those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena that are defilements;
those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena that are both defilements and subject to defilement.

Those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*), are not included among the defilements (*kilesa*) nor among the phenomena associated with defilements (*kilesa-sampayutta*),

but are included by way of the inclusion of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*) and included by way of the inclusion of elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*): how many aggregates and how many bases do those phenomena comprise?
By how many elements (dhātu) are they comprised?
Excluding the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) from the category of aggregates (khandha), those states are comprised by three aggregates, one base (āyatana), and one element.
The three aggregates and likewise the truths (sacca) [are so comprised].
The faculties are sixteen;
in the scheme of conditions,
there are fourteen and then another fourteen.
There are thirty-two items in the ten groups,
and two minor intermediate pairs.
There are eight great sections.
This is the third exposition of terms concerning the uncomprised and the comprised.
